messages:
owen: heads up — after the morning deploy we're seeing OOMs on a bunch of longctx jobs in canary (us-west-2-a). noticed increased RSS and fragmentation in the heap profile. :rotating_light:
li-chen: thanks, looking now. which merge landed? any PR numbers?
owen: PR#4821 changed the eviction window heuristics (shrank soft window to favor earlier eviction). merged ~2h ago, rolled to canary.
tara: I pulled a heap profile from a failing task: pmap shows resident growth spikes aligned with kernel selection switches. suspect the new kernel selector (PR#4860) picking a different matmul kernel + the eviction change is exposing more transient allocs.
jeff: CI perf jobs also flagged RSS regressions — see job 8142. it reports +18MB median RSS for batch path on T4. ci-bot: job 8142 — perf regression detected (rss, allocs) — artifacts: link://ci/8142/artifacts
sam: quick bisect shows tests passing until 4821. when I disable the eviction-change locally, longctx tasks steady. looks like reduced KV window means more frequent evictions which increases compaction churn and fragmentation.
li-chen: I also repro'd a kernel-related scratch growth: the kernel selector now prefers matmul_fused_fp16 for certain seqlen thresholds, it uses a scratch buffer that wasn't accounted for in our kv slab sizing. per run: scratch ~24MB per worker. multiply by 8 workers -> big jump.
owen: sounds like a combinatorial problem: smaller logical cache + bigger kernel scratch -> simultaneous spike OOM. rollout is blocked.
jeff: propose immediate revert of 4821 in canary to stop customer impact, and follow up with a smaller change: keep window but add guard for scratch-aware slab headroom. anyone object?
tara: +1 revert for now. we need an automated check in CI that simulates scratch allocations for kernel variants. otherwise next merge will sneak through.
sam: filing a follow-up: issue #629 — "account for kernel scratch in kv slab sizing and add CI perf probe". will add perf test.
infra-bot: deploy rollback triggered: reverting commit 4821 -> started.
ci-bot: canary-deploy-23: rollback completed. health checks passing on 3/3 canary hosts.
li-chen: after rollback RSS looks back to baseline on my repro runs. fragmentation reduces. I'll prepare a patch that adjusts slab headroom and updates kernel selector to surface scratch size.
owen: thanks. let's keep the rollback in place until we've got a patch + CI probe. we should also add a short runbook note for oncall: "eviction + kernel scratch regressions".
jeff: agreed. I'll post an announcement to eng-runtime with root cause and tracking issue once sam opens #629.
sam: opened #629 with repro, perf artifacts, and suggested patch outline. tagging @li-chen for kernel size detection code.
li-chen: will take it. ETA EOD tomorrow for a PR, unless blocker discovery slows us.
owen: great. filing a post-deploy followup to ensure Dedicated customers' jobs weren't affected beyond canary.
jeff: thanks everyone. moving to P0 until patch lands. :thumbsup:
